item.title: Naomi Osaka 'doesn't give a f---' about US Open outfit hate, says her Haitian 'blood' makes her who she is
item.description: Naomi Osaka fired back at critics on Instagram Threads, comparing the backlash over her bold U.S. Open outfits to scrutiny of her mental health stance.
item.content:encoded:
Naomi Osaka claims she doesn't care about what her critics think of her or her extravagant outfits, but she cares enough to call them out on social media.

The four-time Grand Slam winner donned a number of different, very bold pre-match outfits throughout the U.S. Open, a trend she's set for many years at this point in her career. After being bounced from the tournament in the Round of 16, Osaka had clearly reached her limit of online criticism regarding her ensemble.

"You know…idgaf [I don’t give a f---] if you don’t like me. I don’t mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it," Osaka wrote on Instagram Threads. "This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it’s happening with my clothes lol. I’m literally Haitian it’s in my blood to be this way, as long as the people after me have an easier path it’s worth it."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Osaka was born in Osaka, Japan, and plays under the Japanese flag, but her father, Leonard Francois, is from Jacmel, Haiti, hence her nod to her line about having Haitian blood. She and her family moved from Japan to Long Island, New York, when she was three years old.

Osaka kicked off her 2026 U.S. Open journey by wearing a short-sleeved hoodie, red and black arm sleeves, and a full-length skirt ahead of her first-round match. She also wore a red and black headband around her cornrow-style hair, and later explained that it was a tribute to NBA legend Allen Iverson.

HATERS OF FASHION ATTACK ARYNA SABALENKA WITH 'STREETWALKER' INSULT SIMPLY BECAUSE SHE WORE FISHNET AT US OPEN

Osaka and Nike teamed up for NBA-inspired looks throughout the week, although tipping a cap to Iverson, who has no ties to New York City, the host of the Grand Slam, was a head scratcher. Iverson was also never a Nike athlete during his career.

Ahead of her fourth-round loss to Elena Rybakina, Osaka wore a lavish coat done by KidSuper and a headband with the NBA logo on it before ditching it for a visor during the match.

Osaka infamously wore an outfit she explained was inspired by a jellyfish in a children's book at the Australian Open.

item.title: Israel’s E1 plan explained: The Jerusalem-area corridor sparking international backlash
item.description: Israel says E1 construction in the West Bank falls under the Oslo Accords, but Britain imposed sanctions and 11 nations weigh trade restrictions on settlements.
item.content:encoded:
Israel’s move to advance construction in the strategically significant E1 area between Ma’ale Adumim on the West Bank and Jerusalem has triggered growing backlash, with Britain announcing sanctions and 11 other countries threatening or considering trade restrictions on Jewish communities in the disputed area.

The Netanyahu government last month announced tenders for the first 1,400 of roughly 3,400 housing units in E1, a 4.6-square-mile area that would expand the built-up connection between Ma’ale Adumim, a city of about 40,000 people in the Judean Desert, and the Israeli capital.

European governments have strongly opposed the move, with Britain’s left-wing ruling party announcing sanctions on Tuesday.

BRITAIN’S DRAMATIC CRACKDOWN ON ISRAELI SETTLEMENTS SPARKS FIERCE RESPONSE AS US BLOWBACK LOOMS

The U.K.’s Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, announced a ban on products from Judea and Samaria, saying the government in London "believes the unlawfulness of the occupation should be reflected in the economic relationship we choose to have with the occupied territories."

The foreign ministers of 11 additional countries—Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden—said Tuesday in a joint statement that they intend to impose or are actively considering trade restrictions on goods from Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

Doron Spielman, international spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Office, told Fox News Digital that the E1 project has been underway for years and is located in Area C of the West Bank, which, according to the Oslo Accords, is under full Israeli security and civilian control.

"The Israeli government believes E1 is the natural extension of the area of Ma’ale Adumim, which is an area where Jews live freely within three miles of our biblical capital, Jerusalem. I don’t understand why the world is so focused on a hilltop in the middle of Judea, which is the biblical national homeland of the Jewish people," he said.

Spielman stressed that "at no point in time, in any agreement that Israel ever made, was E1 ever slated to become part of a Palestinian state."

"E1 doesn’t affect Palestinian freedom of movement; that’s a myth. ... Palestinian propaganda is trying to create an international issue about something that is very basic regarding Jews living in their homeland," he added.

HOLY LAND BATTLE: SOLOMON'S POOLS BECOME FLASHPOINT IN FIGHT OVER ISRAEL'S BIBLICAL HERITAGE

While not explicitly commenting on E1, a State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that, as President Donald Trump has made clear, the United States does not support the annexation of the West Bank.

"Such actions could be counterproductive to the President’s Comprehensive Plan to End the Conflict in Gaza and undermine our broader efforts to achieve regional peace and stability," the spokesperson said.

Ashraf al-Ajrami, a former Palestinian Authority minister of Prisoners Affairs, told Fox News Digital that there is no scenario in which the Palestinian Authority would agree to construction in E1.

"The whole international community refutes this plan because they understand the objective of it. It’s not a plan that helps settlers to grow; it’s a plan to destroy the hope of having a two-state solution. It is the opposite of the Palestinian national rights of self-determination and statehood," he said.

"The Israeli government has ignored all the ultimatums from the European Union and even the objections from the American administration up to this point. They will start to build the units merely to divide the Palestinian territories in the West Bank and cut the contiguity between East Jerusalem and our villages in the area," he added.

Former Israeli Ambassador to the United States Michael Oren told Fox News Digital that the E1 project is controversial because the U.S. and other governments that support a two-state solution believe construction there would divide the West Bank and prevent the creation of a Palestinian state.

"The Oslo Accords do not prohibit Israeli settlement construction, nor do they stipulate that the accords’ outcome must be a two-state solution," he said.

"Therefore, this is not a violation of the Oslo Accords. It may violate the spirit of the accords, but there have been many thousands of violations of their spirit. The Second Intifada was a violation of the spirit of the Oslo Accords," he added, referring to the Palestinian terror campaign against Israel from 2000 to 2005, which was marked by suicide bombings targeting civilians.

EXCLUSIVE: ISRAEL SEIZES VAST IRAN TERROR AXIS ARSENAL WITH SURPRISING FOREIGN ORIGINS

Naomi Kahn, international director of Regavim, an NGO dedicated to protecting Israel’s national lands, resources and the rule of law, told Fox News Digital that the Palestinian Authority made the plan controversial 30 years ago when it approached the U.S. administration at the time.

"The Rabin government had actually announced plans to develop the Ma’ale Adumim area, and the PA claimed that if Israel built in E1, it would spell the end of any possibility of a Palestinian state," she said.

While that claim is false in physical terms, Kahn said, it has carried political significance because the PA has made E1 a battleground and involved international actors from the outset.

"E1 has been at the heart of efforts to essentially globalize the push to remove the State of Israel from all of Judea and Samaria," she said.

Kahn noted that some of the countries pushing for sanctions against Israel have spent the past 20 years actively financing and supporting illegal Arab construction in E1, while Palestinian Authority outposts have increasingly mushroomed throughout Judea and Samaria.

She said Regavim first went to court about 16 years ago over the illegal construction of these outposts and has since won six times.

"Still, nothing has happened," said Kahn, whose organization was recently among four Israeli civil society organizations sanctioned by the European Union over allegations that they support "settler violence" and undermine prospects for a Palestinian state.

Dan Diker, president of the Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs, told Fox News Digital that E1 is a critical security corridor that would help protect Jerusalem from Palestinian terrorism and encroachment into areas under Israeli security and administrative control under the Oslo Accords.

Diker said Israel is wary of another invasion following Oct. 7, this time from Palestinian Arab towns, cities and villages across Judea and Samaria.

He claimed, "There are tens of thousands of machine guns, other weapons and ammunition smuggled into Palestinian villages, towns and cities, and there is deep concern that, particularly in communities in the E1 area, they could cut off the road between Jerusalem and Ma’ale Adumim, creating another existential threat," he said.

For the international community, Diker said, the political disagreement over E1 is rooted in the period when Israel and the Palestinian Authority were expected to negotiate the final status of a peace agreement.

"Since then, we’ve had the terror war of 2000, followed by four terror wars waged by Hamas, culminating in Oct. 7. The geopolitical and security reality has completely shifted, but the international community’s mindset has not. For them, it’s a political issue; for us, it’s an existential one," he added.

item.title: Rutgers basketball coach Steve Pikiell reveals that he has cancer, will be sidelined after successful surgery
item.description: Steve Pikiell revealed his cancer diagnosis after successful surgery, with Brandin Knight stepping in as Rutgers interim head coach for now.
item.content:encoded:
Rutgers men’s basketball coach Steve Pikiell announced in a statement Wednesday that he has cancer.

Pikiell, 58, said he began feeling unwell a couple of months ago and went to the doctor.

"A couple of months ago, after not feeling 100 percent, I visited a team of doctors at RWJBarnabas Health. After undergoing various tests, I received the difficult news that I have cancer," Pikiell said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I am incredibly grateful to my team of doctors at RWJBarnabas Health and Memorial Sloan Kettering for guiding and supporting us through this difficult time. After a successful surgery, my doctors and I have a kick-a-- game plan to finish treatment."

Associate head coach Brandin Knight will serve as the interim head coach while Pikiell recovers. Pikiell, who was set to enter his 11th season as the team’s coach, said he will still be involved as much as he can.

"I will still be involved with the team to the best of my ability as I navigate the challenges of the season through treatment. I have great confidence in Coach Knight, the rest of the talented staff, and our exceptional student-athletes. I know they will do an amazing job leading our program when I'm not able to," Pikiell said in the statement.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Just as I ask my team to fight and embrace challenges head-on, I’m going to attack cancer the same way. With the support of my doctors, my family, and now Rutgers Nation, I am confident we will be victorious."

Pikiell thanked the team, Rutgers President William Tate and athletic director Keli Zinn for their support and said he looks forward to being back on the sidelines. Zinn asked that the community lift up Pikiell and his family with encouragement and support.

"On behalf of the Rutgers Athletics family, I want to express our love and support for Coach Pikiell, Kate and their entire family as he fights cancer. Those of us who know Steve, know the determination and strength he brings to everything he does. I know he will bring that same spirit to every treatment and every day ahead," Zinn said in a statement.

"We are grateful to Coach Knight for his willingness to step up during this challenging time and to our entire staff for their great care and compassion for Coach and our student-athletes. There is no set timeline for Coach Pikiell’s full return, but we look forward to the day when he is back on our sideline. I ask that we all lift the Pikiell family with encouragement and support. "

Pikiell has made the NCAA Tournament twice with Rutgers and has a 161-160 record over 321 games with the program. Prior to coaching at Rutgers, Pikiell spent 11 seasons as Stony Brook’s coach.

item.title: Brandi Glanville speaks out on complex diagnosis and $6K monthly medical battle
item.description: Brandi Glanville revealed diagnoses including Klebsiella with biofilm, Valley Fever, Demodex and mononucleosis, facing months of daily IV treatment.
item.content:encoded:
Brandi Glanville is opening up about a series of complex medical diagnoses and the staggering cost of treating a painful condition that has affected her face.

On Tuesday, the former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star – who has been open about a series of health battles over the past couple years – took to social media to reveal she has been diagnosed with highly resistant ESBL Klebsiella and Enterobacter with biofilm, Coccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley Fever, Demodex dermatitis and mononucleosis.

"I’m finally ready to tell you what I’ve actually been fighting and to start sharing some of my worst moments leading up to finally getting diagnosed," she wrote on Instagram, accompanied by a video montage of various stages of her journey.

BRANDI GLANVILLE BELIEVES SHE CONTRACTED 'SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED RINGWORM' IN HER THROAT

In addition to the diagnoses, Glanville said she has a "fungal ball" in her face that needs to be surgically removed. She also expects to undergo procedures to remove metals from old dental work and breast implants.

"I’m looking at 4-6 months of daily IV treatment," she wrote.

PAMELA ANDERSON REVEALS SHE DRAINED HER BANK ACCOUNT TO BEAT HEPATITIS C

Glanville said the treatment has been difficult and that she has seen "very little improvement" so far. She added that the medical battle is expected to cost between $3,300 and $6,000 per month.

"I’m not able to work right now other than my podcast and I honestly don’t know how I’m going to do this mentally or financially," she admitted.

'FULL HOUSE' STAR DAVE COULIER REVEALS 45-POUND WEIGHT LOSS, GRUELING SIDE EFFECTS FROM CANCER FIGHTS

The reality star has previously said she receives IV infusions for as many as 18 hours a day. The grueling treatments have made it difficult for her to sleep, eat and participate in normal activities.

"I just want this s--- out of my body," Glanville wrote. "I want my health back. I want my life back. I want to feel like me again."

Glanville also addressed the videos and photos she shared showing the physical toll of her illness.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I know I don’t look good in these videos," she wrote. "Honestly, I don’t care. I feel terrible and this is what being sick looks like for me right now. So please be nice in the comments. I’m already fighting enough."

Glanville previously shared that she believed she picked up a parasite after visiting Morocco in 2023. She suffered from facial paralysis and initially was diagnosed with stress-induced angioedema.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Glanville previously told Fox News Digital that while no one had figured out what was truly wrong with her disfigured face, doctors had suggested "that it could be a parasite, but they're not sure."

Angioedema "is a reaction similar to hives that affects deeper layers of the skin. It can appear with hives or alone," according to the Mayo Clinic. Her symptoms remained, and in fact became worse. Glanville wasn't convinced angioedema was the problem, and put her health at the forefront of her mind in pursuit of an answer.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

In February, the reality star discovered that her 20-year-old ruptured breast implants were to blame for her medical issues.

Prior to the revelation, Glanville admitted she spent more than $70,000 in an attempt to find an answer to the medical mystery that consumed her everyday experience and disfigured her face.

Fox News Digital's Tracy Wright contributed to this post.

item.title: Emergency slide sparks questions on Trump’s new Air Force One before president reveals why
item.description: An emergency slide deployed from the Qatar-gifted Boeing 747 at Joint Base Andrews before Trump explained it was part of a routine safety check.
item.content:encoded:
An emergency slide deployment on the Qatari-gifted Air Force One raised questions at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday before President Donald Trump revealed it was all part of a safety check.

"They were checking it before, and they just wanted to make sure," Trump told reporters on the tarmac after exiting Marine One. "So they’ve, I guess, already put it up. They want to make sure everything works perfectly."

The unusual scene unfolded after Marine One rolled to a stop near the presidential aircraft, with Trump remaining aboard the helicopter, and the slide could be seen extending from the plane.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SUBPOENAS NY TIMES JOURNALISTS IN GRAND JURY LEAK PROBE TIED TO AIR FORCE ONE REPORT

The White House print pool reported spotting what appeared to be an inflatable emergency slide deployed from the right side front door of the Qatari-gifted Boeing 747. The door is opposite the entrance Trump typically uses to board the plane.

At the same time, the older white-and-blue Air Force One was seen moving out of its hangar and into position a few hundred yards behind the newer aircraft. The older jet then deployed its front and rear stairs.

TRUMP EXPLAINS WHY HE'S FLYING OLD AIR FORCE ONE BACK TO DC

The door of Marine One remained closed as of 2:19 p.m., according to the pool, fueling questions about whether the unexpected slide deployment had disrupted the president’s travel plans.

Trump later emerged from the helicopter and said the equipment had been tested to ensure it was working properly, indicating there had not been an emergency aboard the aircraft.

It was not immediately clear whether the safety check would affect which plane Trump would use for his next flight.

Fox News' Nick Rojas contributed to this report.

item.title: 'Alien harboring' accusations fly as DC-area county spends taxpayer funds to blunt ICE
item.description: A Virginia county faces fire for a new policy providing taxpayer-funded grants to families of illegal immigrants whose breadwinner was deported by ICE.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A Virginia county is under fire for a new policy providing taxpayer funds in the form of grants to families of illegal immigrants whose breadwinner was detained or deported by ICE.

Arlington County, which sits just across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C., is not new to policies critics say interfere with DHS operations, as it previously caused outrage when the chair of the Arlington County board publicly suggested residents call police to report ICE sightings in January.

"If you look at the alien harboring statute – do you do anything to encourage or induce people to either come illegally or that are illegally here to stay, that could be arguably a violation of the alien harboring statute?" former acting ICE Director Jonathan Fahey told Fox News Digital in a Wednesday interview.

DOJ THREATENS TO CUT BILLIONS IN WELFARE FUNDING FROM STATES FOR FAILING TO REPORT ILLEGAL MIGRANTS

"By giving money to people… the reasonable inference is that these people are also illegal, the money enables them to stay in the country illegally, because they lost their breadwinner," Fahey said.

He said Arlington County Manager Mark Schwartz’s comments to ARLNow that many of the affected families are "unbanked" – or lack access to financial institutions which statutorily require identification to open deposit accounts – is itself a tell.

TAXPAYER-FUNDED HOUSING FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IN GOP'S CROSSHAIRS: 'IT'S GOT TO STOP'

"That shows the county knows the money is going to be going to people that are illegally here and it will help them stay. So that's where I think the alien harboring statute comes into play," he said, adding the county shows "reckless disregard" for the fact their policies accommodate people in the country illegally.

Arlington will start by setting aside $50,000 to be distributed through "social safety-net" ministry ArlingtonThrive in increments of up to $2,000 per affected family to cover basic needs and utilities, according to reports.

The plan – which passed 4-0 with one board member absent – reportedly formed after a major ICE operation in Maryland and Virginia netted 1,328 illegal immigrant arrests, including the case of a man who ran from agents when confronted near the U.S. Air Force Memorial.

Five regional federal Democrats sounded off afterward, endorsing an ensuing Arlington County Police investigation into the encounter between ICE and Jose Mejia Hernandez, who was reportedly tased and suffered a brain bleed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Arlington County officials, including Chairman Matt de Ferranti, a Democrat from Rock Spring.

"We are valuing the families of those that have been displaced and removed," he told local press.

In January, de Ferranti warned Arlingtonians that county law prohibits its "public safety professionals" from "interfering with enforcement of federal immigration law," but that his suggestion to call 911 to report ICE sightings helps officials know agents are present and pivot to "pursu[ing] Arlington County’s law enforcement mission: preventing violence in our community."

DOJ ACCUSES MARYLAND OF 'ACTIVE AND DELIBERATE EFFORT' TO PREVENT DEPORTATIONS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS: LAWSUIT

Reckless disregard and inducement are both subsections of the law Fahey referenced – 8 U.S.C. 1324.

Leadership at the Department of Homeland Security was similarly critical of Arlington’s move.

"You can’t make this up," an agency spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

"Sanctuary politicians are taking Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars to reward illegal aliens who break the law. This insanity shows once again who they put first."

Fahey said counties cannot make their own immigration laws, and with Arlington in particular, their alleged "inducement" doesn’t just affect their county, as creating safe harbor for illegal immigrants can have ripple effects in adjacent areas like the District of Columbia, cities of Falls Church and Alexandria and Fairfax County.

"A person could go on and commit another crime somewhere outside of Arlington… you can’t have localities and states carving out their own immigration laws or saying immigration laws can’t be enforced [here]."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Arguments against mass deportation on the grounds of family separation are similarly flawed, the former director said, pointing to the fact that when an American citizen is arrested or jailed, they are also physically "separated" from their family.

"Latest dispatch from the People’s Republic of Arlington," read a critical posting on X.

item.title: Mamdani, NYPD give security update ahead of Jewish High Holy Days, 9/11 25th anniversary
item.description: Zohran Mamdani and Jessica Tisch announced an increased NYPD presence at synagogues across New York City as antisemitic hate crimes rise ahead of holy days.
item.content:encoded:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and New York Police Department (NYPD) Commissioner Jessica Tisch revealed increased security measures ahead of September's Jewish High Holy Days and ceremonies to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

During a press conference Wednesday, Mamdani discouraged the public from traversing through lower Manhattan on Friday. The city will be closing streets around Ground Zero with dignitaries, including Vice President JD Vance, slated to attend a commemoration of the 25th anniversary of 9/11.

The mayor also expressed sympathy to Jewish New Yorkers who have experienced an uptick in antisemitic hate crimes in recent years.

"I want to speak directly to our Jewish New Yorkers now," Mamdani said. "Your safety during these sacred days is of the utmost importance to our administration, and we will work tirelessly to ensure that you can observe the holiday securely. There will be an increased NYPD presence outside of synagogues across the five boroughs, as well as other Jewish religious and cultural locations."

MAN CHARGED WITH ASSAULT, HATE CRIMES AFTER ALLEGEDLY DISRUPTING SHABBAT SERVICES AT NYC SYNAGOGUE

Mamdani said there were no specific or credible threats to any New Yorkers but maintained that the city will remain vigilant ahead of the weekend's events.

Tisch echoed Mamdani's message that there were no specific threats, adding that hate crimes, and antisemitic hate crimes in particular, are on the rise.

ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE ESCALATES AS DEADLY WEAPON ATTACKS SURGE IN 2025: REPORT

"Even as shootings and murders have fallen to historic lows, hate crimes are moving in the wrong direction through the first eight months of this year. Confirmed hate crimes citywide are up 16%, and antisemitic hate crimes are up 9%. And once again, more than half of all confirmed hate crimes in New York City have targeted Jewish New Yorkers, even though Jews make up only about 10% of this city's population. Those numbers are deeply disturbing," Tisch said.

She pointed to specific incidents, including the July stabbing of Moshe Grunhaus, a 50-year-old Jewish man wearing a kippah who was attacked with a screwdriver outside The Jewish Center in Manhattan's Upper West Side.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

She also revealed that intelligence officers have disrupted multiple plotted attacks on Jews in New York in recent years.

"Since October 7th, our intelligence community has also tracked threats and disrupted plots directed at Jewish institutions here in New York, including alleged plans for attacks against a Manhattan synagogue and a Jewish center in Brooklyn," Tisch said.

Tisch assured New York's Jews that they can rely on the NYPD to protect them.

"I want all Jewish New Yorkers to know this. You have a partner in the NYPD now and throughout the year. As of today, there are no specific, credible threats directed at High Holy Day celebrations in New York City. But we remain vigilant," she said.

Fox News Digital contacted the mayor's office and the NYPD for additional comment.

item.title: Amazon's Alexa can now verify suspicious messages
item.description: Amazon's Alexa for Shopping now lets customers verify suspicious emails, texts and phone calls against the company's own communication records.
item.content:encoded:
We have seen plenty of scams borrow Amazon's name, and some of them look convincing enough to make almost anyone hesitate.

Earlier this summer, we showed you a fake Amazon email that claimed there was unusual activity on an account and pushed the recipient to "Sign In to Verify." The message even suggested a document might need to be uploaded. We have also warned about fake Amazon recruiting texts promising hundreds of dollars a day for easy remote work.

The stories change, but scammers keep coming back to Amazon because so many of us use it. A delivery warning or account alert can feel believable when you are already expecting a package.

Now Amazon is giving customers a new way to answer the question we keep asking when these messages arrive: Did Amazon actually send this? The company says about 360,000 customers contact Amazon customer service every year asking whether a message is real. Its latest answer is built into Alexa for Shopping.

AMAZON JOB SCAM TEXTS ARE SPREADING AGAIN WITH A NEW TWIST

Here is how the new verification tool works, what it can tell you and why you should still keep your guard up when an Amazon message feels suspicious.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

Amazon says U.S. customers can now ask Alexa for Shopping whether an email, text, phone call or other message actually came from Amazon. Alexa for Shopping is Amazon's AI shopping assistant. It helps customers find products, compare items and manage shopping through natural conversation. Prime membership is not required to use Alexa for Shopping, but if you are considering joining, see our guide on how to get a cheap Amazon Prime membership at Cyberguy.com.

Now, you can also use Alexa for Shopping when something suspicious lands on your phone or computer. Instead of trying to judge a message by appearance alone, you can describe it to Alexa for Shopping.

You might ask: "Did Amazon send me a text about a delivery problem yesterday?" Or you could ask whether a Prime membership email came from Amazon. You can even provide details about a phone call from someone claiming to offer an Amazon refund. The verification tool then checks the information you provide against Amazon's own communication records.

When you ask Alexa for Shopping about a suspicious communication, provide details about where it came from and when you received it. You can also tell the assistant what the message said. Amazon then compares those details with its records.

According to the company, its technology looks at information such as the sender and message content. It also considers timing and formatting.

That gives Amazon an advantage over tools that simply search for suspicious wording or potentially dangerous links. Amazon can compare the communication with messages generated through its own systems. The company says it only confirms a message as legitimate when the tool has complete confidence.

The answer depends on what Amazon finds. If Amazon can match the communication to its records, Alexa for Shopping tells you it came from Amazon. It can also provide details about the communication and account security advice.

If the message does not match Amazon's records, the tool tells you that the information provided does not appear to correspond with an official Amazon communication.

At that point, Amazon may advise you to check your orders directly in the app or contact Amazon through its official support channels. You should also avoid clicking links in the suspicious message.

There is another possibility. Alexa may tell you that it cannot verify the communication with certainty. If that happens, Amazon provides additional steps. You can submit more detailed information or use another Amazon verification option.

AMAZON RECALL TEXT SCAM COMES WITH RED FLAGS

Alexa for Shopping is only one of Amazon's verification options. Earlier this year, Amazon launched verify@amazon.com. Anyone worldwide can forward a suspicious message to that email address and receive a response about whether Amazon sent it. You do not need an Amazon account or the Amazon app to use the service.

Amazon also offers a communication verification form through its customer service pages. So, if Alexa for Shopping cannot give you a firm answer, you still have another way to check before taking action.

There is another interesting part of the new feature. When you ask Alexa for Shopping to verify a communication, Amazon says it automatically reports that submission to its customer protection and enforcement team.

Those reports can help Amazon identify developing scam campaigns and bad actors impersonating the company. That means the suspicious text sitting on your phone could potentially help Amazon spot a larger scam targeting other customers.

Amazon scams work because they often start with something completely believable. You ordered something last week, so a delivery problem sounds possible. You have a Prime membership, so an account warning gets your attention. Then the scammer adds pressure.

A fake email may claim your account has been locked. Another message might say someone placed an expensive order using your account. That urgency can push you toward a link before you have time to think.

We saw exactly that pattern in the fake Amazon account email we investigated. The message used Amazon branding and warned that the account had been placed on hold. The safest response remains simple. Do not use the link in the message to investigate the warning. Open Amazon yourself and check your account.

FBI HELPS TAKE DOWN AI PHISHING RING

Amazon's new verification feature gives you another way to check suspicious communications. However, scammers will keep changing their tactics, so these steps can help you stay safer.

Be cautious when a message pressures you to act immediately or threatens consequences if you do not respond. Scammers want you reacting quickly because slowing down gives you more time to spot something suspicious.

If a message claims your account will close or a package requires immediate action, avoid clicking its links. Check your Amazon account through the official app or website instead.

Watch for anyone claiming to represent Amazon who asks you to buy gift cards as payment. Amazon warns that it will never ask you to purchase a gift card to resolve an account problem or make a payment. If someone makes that request, stop communicating with them.

Be especially careful if a caller asks for sensitive account information. Amazon says it will never ask for your password or one-time passcode over the phone. If someone claiming to represent Amazon asks for those details, end the conversation and contact Amazon through an official channel.

Phone scams deserve extra caution because the number on your screen can look convincing. Scammers can spoof caller ID information and make a call appear to come from a familiar company. Seeing "Amazon" on your phone does not prove Amazon is actually calling. If someone unexpectedly calls about a refund or account problem, avoid giving them information. Hang up and check your Amazon account independently.

Phishing messages can expose you to malicious websites and dangerous downloads. That is why I recommend using strong antivirus software on your devices. Strong antivirus software can warn you about known phishing sites and suspicious links. It can also help detect malware if a scammer tricks you into downloading something dangerous. item.title: Mina Kimes thinks perception of Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal is unfair to women
item.description: Mina Kimes says the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel scandal gives bad-faith actors license to target women working in sports media nationwide.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN analyst Mina Kimes says the scandal involving former NFL reporter Dianna Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has given bad-faith actors an excuse to target women.

For background, an ESPN report earlier this week cited anonymous female reporters who claimed the scandal has caused them to navigate their jobs differently.

"One reporter said an assistant coach told her he would not want to be seen meeting her for a coffee, specifically citing the optics of the Vrabel-Russini situation," ESPN reported.

Kimes discussed the report on a podcast with Charlotte Wilder this week, accusing fans of creating a negative narrative around women in sports.

"I think it reflects sort of a broader thing that happens in any industry, which is when someone who’s not in the majority makes any sort of error, it becomes a referendum for their entire class," Kimes said.

She added that critics are not applying the same standards to other insiders.

"Giving license to male sports fans generally to speak about them a certain way, or to honestly talk about this story in a way that they don’t with other stories involving lapses in journalism. It’s been interesting to watch on the Russini side of it, this massive conversation on the internet about, ‘This is a crime against journalism, and no one’s talking about it’ … it’s kind of hard to take those critiques in good faith when they’re clearly not coming from a place of, these aren’t people who actually care about journalism." Kimes added.

Wilder took a more pointed stance, accusing fans of misogyny.

"It seems to me that to blame one woman for making a mistake and saying that she has screwed it up for everybody else, nobody does that for men," Wilder said. "I understand that it is different; she was in a very high-profile position, but it doesn’t sit right, I don’t think."

"It gives license to people, perhaps, who are looking for an excuse to not treat women the same way, and then run with it," she added.

Got all that?

MATTHEW BERRY DISCUSSES WHETHER HE'D HIRE DIANNA RUSSINI FOR HIS BUDDING FANTASY FOOTBALL EMPIRE

It is also understandable that male officials around the league would now be more cognizant of spending time alone with female reporters, given the potential narratives.

Granted, these dynamics were in place long before photos surfaced of Russini hugging and holding hands with a current football coach. The perception of relationships between men and women will always be viewed differently by some observers.

The same would be true if a male reporter were alone with a female coach in the WNBA.

We would, however, push back on Wilder’s claim that Russini "screwed it up" for all women. While coaches and officials might be more careful around female reporters, the general view of women in the industry has not changed.

No honest media executive or source thinks differently of Stacey Dales, Charissa Thompson, Laura Rutledge, Erin Andrews, Sage Steele or other top women in sports media because of Russini’s photos.

Kimes and Wilder seem to be, predictably, putting too much stock in what anonymous social media trolls post.

For example, ESPN reporter Taylor McGregor gained national attention this week for her stellar on-air reporting during the Florida State-SMU power outage. No serious person questioned her credentials because Russini allegedly spent time on a boat with Vrabel while she was seven months pregnant.

item.title: Missouri Supreme Court threatens secretary of state with contempt amid intensifying redistricting battle
item.description: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins must appear Thursday to explain why he shouldn't be held in contempt over Missouri's congressional maps battle.
item.content:encoded:
The Missouri Supreme Court signaled Tuesday that it was considering holding Secretary of State Denny Hoskins in contempt amid an escalating battle over proposed congressional maps.

Hoskins, a Republican, said Tuesday that he would keep using the congressional districts redrawn last year, despite a U.S. Supreme Court decision that left standing a state Supreme Court order requiring Missouri to use its old districts instead.

"I look forward to my day in court," Hoskins said in a post on X that cited the supremacy clause of the U.S. Constitution.

MISSOURI AG FILES PETITION ASKING SUPREME COURT TO REVIVE TRUMP-BACKED REDISTRICTING MAP

Hoskins must appear in court Thursday to explain why he shouldn't be held in contempt for instructing election officials to use the 2025 congressional map despite an injunction barring its use.

Last week, Missouri's high court ruled that the map backed by President Donald Trump cannot be used because thousands of voters signed a petition demanding a statewide referendum on it.

SUPREME COURT DEALS BLOW TO VIRGINIA DEMOCRATS IN FIGHT OVER STATE COURT ELECTION MAP RULING

Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh declined to grant an emergency stay requested by Hoskins, leaving in place the injunction ordered by the state Supreme Court.

However, shortly after Kavanaugh's announcement, U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark, a Trump appointee, issued a temporary restraining order prohibiting Missouri from using any map other than the new 2025 districts.

GEORGIA REDISTRICTING BATTLE REVIVED AFTER APPEALS COURT OVERTURNS FEDERAL COURT DECISION

Opponents of the new redistricting plan quickly filed a notice to appeal Clark's order to the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

"An individual federal judge cannot overrule the Missouri Supreme Court," said attorney Chuck Hatfield, who represents People Not Politicians, the group that sponsored the referendum petition.

RNC AND NRCC FILE LAWSUIT DEFENDING MISSOURI'S NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAP AGAINST DEMOCRATIC CHALLENGES

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway said she was prepared to comply with Clark's order, which she argued "binds the state to using" the new congressional districts.

"We maintain that changing the congressional map in between the primary and general elections is simply not feasible and profoundly unjust to Missouri voters," she wrote on X.

BLOCKBUSTER SUPREME COURT VOTING RIGHTS RULING IGNITES REDISTRICTING WAR ACROSS SOUTHERN STATES

The conflict is part of a broader, nationwide effort by Republicans to redraw congressional districts mid-decade to gain U.S. House seats.

Missouri currently has six Republicans and two Democrats in the U.S. House. The new redistricting plan would eliminate one Democratic seat, currently held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Ahead of GOP convention, Dallas Dems share worried optimism
item.description: James Talarico faces an enthusiasm gap at the Dallas Labor Day rally as his Texas senate race against Ken Paxton heats up with new ad money.
item.content:encoded:
There were a few hundred Democrats gathered at a venue called Lofty Spaces in Dallas on Monday, in a sweltering heat that could not hold back the annual Labor Day political rally. And while on the surface all was confidence, when you scratched a little deeper, you struck frayed nerves.

Ellen, a retired nurse who sometimes protests in a Statue of Liberty costume, was there, and agreed to an interview if I helped to take her gear to her car, which I would have done anyway, of course.

Ellen was optimistic about Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico in his race against Republican Ken Paxton.

"I feel very good about him, I’m very optimistic, I don’t think Texans are going to vote for a criminal, cheat, adulterer, Ken Paxton," she said.

When I pointed out that Paxton, the current state attorney general, had already won statewide elections twice, she smiled and said, "That’s the problem."

But not the only problem. Asked about Talarico’s Senate primary opponent, Rep. Jasmine Crockett, a high-profile Black Texas Democrat who has thus far refused to back Talarico, Ellen said, "I voted for her, and after he won…and she decided she wasn’t going to support him, I was so glad that she lost.

JASMINE CROCKETT BLASTS HER TEXAS DEMOCRATIC PRIMARY LOSS AS ‘RACIST RACE'

Joanna and Ruth, who are in Ellen's age demo and also very active in the Democratic Party in Dallas, thought Talarico is looking good.

,"I’m feeling more encouraged than I have in a really long time, that it is going to flip over," Joanna added, "I’m feeling really fabulous about it too," but again, concerns over Crockett and the Black vote lingered.

Joanna shared that, "I really hope she gets on board to help with the Black people, because we need them voting, but she has always been my rep and I love her."

Several Black Democrats I spoke with at the event felt confident that Crockett’s obstinance would not be decisive, and were not willing to attack her for it.

Perhaps the biggest headwind for Talarico that I discovered in Dallas, something that polling has a hard time catching up to, is a lack of enthusiasm over him. Determination to win is in the air, but far less so is excitement.

Later that day, downtown, I met Richard who is in his 30s and works in the service industry. He said there was more buzz in the lead-up to Beto O’Rourke’s narrow 2018 Senate loss,

"The energy for Beto was everywhere, it was palpable," he said. "I was sure that Ted Cruz was going to lose. I don’t feel that this time."

Jaime, a liberal elementary school principal, seemed a bit less worried about the energy gap, though he did acknowledge, "Beto had style and rizz, Talarico is kind of a square."

And let’s face it, back in 2018, we even had a term for O’Rourke’s appeal: ‘Beto-Mania.' There is no Talarico-Mania.

I wound up asking several people this question, and even those who shrugged it off only did so after a look in their eyes told me they knew it was at least a real thing, if not a dealbreaker.

Meanwhile, the massive on-hand money advantage that Talarico has enjoyed is starting to evaporate, as President Trump’s PAC this week committed $10 million to back Paxton. Republican Gov. Greg Abbott’s ads, focused on oil production and culture issues, also serve as de facto anti-Talarico spots.

On final bump in the road for Talarico is that in Texas, even among many Democrats, immigration is a tricky issue. Unlike in places like Michigan and Virginia, Democrats in Dallas were not saying they want to abolish ICE, but rather reform it. They do not want a return to Joe Biden’s policies on the southern border.

Well do they recall the 15,000 Haitians lined up at the border in Del Rio, under Grandpa Joe’s watch.

Curiously, a name that did not come up very often in my discussions with Democratic voters was Donald Trump, and after a decade of hearing little else from them, that was a bit jarring.

REPUBLICAN PARTY TO HOST HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION IN DALLAS, TRUMP ANNOUNCES ON TRUTH SOCIAL

Voters on the Left are realizing that they can’t simply run against Trump anymore, because The Donald is in the home stretch of his presidency. Time will succeed, where their party failed, in ending Trump’s tenure in the White House. The real question is, what comes next?

Will Texas be fool's gold for the Democrats again this year, as it has so often been, or will the new demography of blue state transplants finally get them over the top? For now, as Republicans are set to make their pitch in Dallas this week, the feeling is more one of worry than outright confidence.

item.title: NYPD chief: 9/11 heroes’ legacy lives on in every generation of officers
item.description: The NYPD memorial wall at One Police Plaza honors 23 officers killed on 9/11 and hundreds more lost to World Trade Center-related illnesses.
item.content:encoded:
The legacy of the NYPD officers who ran toward danger on Sept. 11, 2001, continues to shape the department a quarter-century later, Chief of Department Michael LiPetri said during a ceremony dedicating a memorial wall to members who died in the attacks and their aftermath.

"None of us gets here alone," LiPetri said. "Whatever rank we reach, whatever command we lead, we are standing on the foundations other people built."

"We inherit their lessons, their example, and eventually it becomes our responsibility to pass those things forward," he added.

FOX NEWS MEDIA ANNOUNCES EXTENSIVE 9/11 ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE FROM GROUND ZERO, PENTAGON AND SHANKSVILLE

The NYPD has lost more than 469 members to illnesses connected to their service after the attacks, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said. More than 1,700 members have retired from the department with World Trade Center-related disabilities, LiPetri added.

"We are still losing members to illnesses caused by their service after the attacks," LiPetri said. "All these years later, we are still standing with families as they bury loved ones whose lives were forever changed by the work they did after Sept. 11."

9/11 VICTIM'S IDENTITY EMERGES NEARLY 25 YEARS LATER AFTER DNA BREAKTHROUGH CRACKS MYSTERY

The memorial wall at One Police Plaza honors the 23 NYPD officers killed at the World Trade Center that morning, along with members who later died from illnesses linked to their rescue and recovery efforts.

"Sept. 11 did not end on Sept. 11," NYPD Chief Chaplain Rev. A.R. Bernard said during the invocation. "For many, the costs continued for years, illness endured, families impacted and lives ultimately lost."

FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' -- THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE

Mayor Zohran Mamdani recalled the story of Officer John William Perry, who was at One Police Plaza preparing to resign and begin a career as an attorney when the first plane struck the North Tower. Perry asked for his shield back and rushed to the World Trade Center.

"There he was confronted with unimaginable suffering, but he did not stop with the same immense bravery and courage that was commonplace among so many that day, the kind that has long defined this department," Mamdani said.

"Officer Perry ran into the fire. The last time he was seen he was helping a woman out of the South Tower before rushing back in to save as many others as he could. Officer Perry and 22 of his fellow officers, each with their own stories, were killed that morning. That includes 14 members of the emergency service unit, who were among the first to enter the towers."

TRUMP POSTHUMOUSLY AWARDS MEDAL OF FREEDOM TO 9/11'S 'MAN IN RED BANDANA'

Mamdani noted that the sons of officers Ronnie Klopfer and Joseph Viviano "now carry on his legacy of bravery as valued members of this very department."

"Every officer present that day embodied the NYPD’s creed that the duty to protect is not a job that one clocks out of, but a calling," Mamdani said. "One answers until the very end.

"In the days and months that followed Sept. 11, thousands of NYPD officers and staff from across every precinct and every borough heeded that same call. They took on that same heavy and incalculable risk."

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: 9/11 IS JUST A HISTORY CHAPTER FOR A NEW GENERATION OF AMERICANS

Their sons play on the same lacrosse team Klopfer founded before the attacks.

"Their fathers are gone, but the team that Ron built is still here," LiPetri said. "Their sons are wearing an NYPD uniform, and a connection that began years before Sept. 11 continues inside the department."

Tisch said thousands of current NYPD officers were children on 9/11, while many others had not yet been born. She said preserving the memories of those who served is becoming increasingly important as the generation that responded to the attacks retires.

"The faces in this building will be different, but these names will still be here," Tisch said. "The example of the men and women behind them will continue to shape the department."

New York Liberty star and WNBA legend Breanna Stewart is leading Team USA’s pursuit of a fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup title, and appears proud to represent the red, white and blue while doing it.

THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE

Stewart’s history with USA Basketball stretches back to 2009, when she competed at the U16 level as a 14-year-old. She has since won three Olympic gold medals and three World Cup championships. She was also named MVP of the 2018 World Cup.

A championship in Berlin would give Stewart a fourth World Cup title and extend one of the most dominant runs in sports history.

The U.S. went undefeated in group play, although its 55-52 escape against Italy exposed some vulnerability. Stewart then led the Americans with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists in a 105-64 victory over Czechia.

Stewart has not avoided political activism herself. She held an "Abolish ICE" sign before an Unrivaled game in January and has long spoken publicly about social justice and LGBTQ rights.

item.title: Nike forgot that Republicans buy sneakers, too, and now it's getting booted from the S&P 100
item.description: Michael Jordan's famous sneakers quote haunts Nike as the brand exits the S&P 100 after a stunning $200 billion collapse tied to left-wing politics.
item.content:encoded:
"Republicans buy sneakers, too."

Those famous words came from Michael Jordan, widely regarded as the greatest basketball player of all time. He was also the athlete most responsible for transforming Nike from a shoe company into a global sports empire.

Jordan made the comment during the 1990 U.S. Senate race in North Carolina, after his mother urged him to support Democratic candidate Harvey Gantt and record a public-service announcement. Jordan confirmed in ESPN’s "The Last Dance" that he made the remark jokingly on a team bus.

Maybe so. But the line endured because it captured a basic business lesson in four words. Republicans buy shoes. Democrats buy shoes. Most companies benefit when both groups want to buy theirs.

Nike stopped listening.

FROM COLIN KAEPERNICK TO DYLAN MULVANEY, NIKE'S DECADE OF LEFT-WING ACTIVISM HAS FINALLY CAUGHT UP TO IT

After spending much of the past decade injecting left-wing politics into its brand, Nike is now set to be removed from the S&P 100, ending a run of nearly 18 years in the blue-chip index. S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the move Friday, and Nike will come out before trading begins Sept. 21.

S&P isn’t kicking Nike out because the index committee hated the Kaepernick ad or saw Dylan Mulvaney in a sports bra. Nike is getting kicked out because its value collapsed.

The politics didn’t wipe out $200 billion by itself. But Nike volunteered to alienate customers while it was already losing ground everywhere else.

The sports apparel giant reached a market value of approximately $281 billion near its November 2021 peak. Nike shares closed Tuesday at $38.10, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $56.5 billion. The stock was about 79% below its Nov. 5, 2021 intraday record of $179.10, and more than $220 billion in market value had disappeared.

Getting removed from the S&P 100 won’t put Nike out of business. It will still sell billions of dollars in shoes and sign some of the biggest athletes in the world.

But Nike used to look untouchable. Now it’s worth about one-fifth of what it was five years ago and no longer has a spot in one of America’s premier blue-chip indexes.

China is where this story gets really good.

Nike made Colin Kaepernick the face of its 30th-anniversary "Just Do It" campaign after he refused to stand for the national anthem, saying he wouldn’t show pride in a country that "oppresses Black people and people of color."

Nike apparently thought that was a message worth putting on billboards across America.

Contrast that with how the company publicly talked about China.

In 2021, Nike faced backlash from Chinese consumers after the company expressed concern about reports of forced labor involving Uyghurs in Xinjiang. During an earnings call a few months later, then-CEO John Donahoe made Nike’s priorities clear.

"We’re a brand of China and for China," Donahoe said.

Quite a difference, isn’t it? Nike had plenty to say about oppression when the target was the United States. But when the company’s business in an actual communist country came under pressure, its CEO reminded everyone that Nike had been investing there for more than 40 years, operated thousands of stores and remained committed to the Chinese market.

Nike was perfectly willing to embrace anti-American messaging at home while continuing to grow in China by assuring Chinese consumers that the company was "of China and for China."

It didn’t work.

MARY CAIN'S BOOK AND NIKE'S TRANS-ATHLETE STUDY REVEAL THE SAME PATTERN OF CORPORATE HYPOCRISY

When Donahoe made that declaration in 2021, Nike generated $8.29 billion in Greater China. Five years later, that number is down to $5.85 billion. Nearly 30% of the business disappeared, including an 11% drop in the past year.

So much for being "of China and for China."

In 2019, Nike pulled a Fourth of July-themed Air Max sneaker featuring the Betsy Ross flag because it said the design could "unintentionally offend." A year later, the company launched its "For Once, Don’t Do It" racial-justice campaign and publicly embraced Black Lives Matter messaging.

Then Nike partnered with Dylan Mulvaney in 2023 for a paid promotion of women’s leggings and sports bras. Also, OutKick reported that researchers and a Boston Children’s Hospital publication had described Nike as supporting a proposed study involving transgender youth athletes. A Nike executive, speaking to OutKick on background, later said the study "was never initialized" and was "not moving forward," while researcher Joanna Harper subsequently said Nike had pulled out after critics learned of it.

Nike made left-wing politics part of its identity and repeatedly dared customers to object.

Now Nike is leaving the S&P 100, its stock is down nearly 80% from its peak and its executives are trying to rebuild the product innovation and marketplace relationships that once made the company dominant.

Michael Jordan understood that Republicans buy sneakers, too.

He also understood something Nike forgot: They don’t have to buy yours.

item.title: Can Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride carry the Cardinals offense under new coach Mike LaFleur?
item.description: Mike LaFleur takes over as Arizona Cardinals head coach with Jacoby Brissett under center after the franchise parted ways with Kyler Murray.
item.content:encoded:
When a franchise moves on from a former No. 1 overall pick at quarterback, resets its coaching staff, and embraces a complete roster transformation, establishing a baseline level of execution becomes the ultimate priority. With former 49ers offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur stepping in as head coach and veteran signal-caller Jacoby Brissett taking over under center, Arizona is aiming to establish a culture of accountability and rebuild its foundation in a relentless division.

The Cardinals endured a miserable 2025 campaign, finishing last in the NFC West with a 3–14 record. To build out the depth chart under LaFleur, the Cardinals brought in wide receivers Kendrick Bourne and Devin Duvernay alongside running back Tyler Allgeier. None of these moves are going to make this team a playoff team, but it will at least make them potentially competitive. It should also give LeFleur a chance to showcase what he can do and what areas the team needs to improve.

Marvin Harrison Jr., Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and All-Pro caliber tight end Trey McBride give the offense a bit of hope. However, there are a lot of questions about these players. item.description: Interim Chief Andre Sayles unveiled a strategy targeting known "trigger pullers" after three deadly Seattle shootings over Labor Day weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle’s interim police chief referred to known gun-violence suspects as "trigger pullers" during a Labor Day weekend news conference where he discussed three separate shootings and his department’s response.

Three people were killed, and three others were injured in the shootings over a 24-hour stretch, FOX 13 Seattle reported.

Interim Chief Andre Sayles said the Seattle Police Department was increasing patrols, coordinating with business owners, and deploying its community response group and gun violence reduction unit to curb the violence.

SEATTLE MAYOR KATIE WILSON NAMES ANDRE SAYLES AS INTERIM POLICE CHIEF AFTER BARNES RESIGNATION

"We’re looking at ways to where we can identify individuals that are known, we call trigger pullers, in our community," Sayles said during a Sept. 7 briefing. "Identifying them, making sure that we’re putting cases on those individuals working with King County Prosecutor’s Office, to bring these individuals to justice, because the families that lost loved ones, throughout the year and years past, deserve justice."

Seattle police told Fox News Digital on Wednesday that "trigger puller" is an informal term and is not required by department policy.

The term drew pushback from local commentators who said it softened the description of violent suspects.

"So in Seattle we aren’t calling them ‘shooters’ anymore? Now they are ‘trigger pullers’?" local radio host Ari Hoffman posted on social media following Sayles’ remarks.

The phrase is not new to law enforcement. In 2022, then-FBI Director Christopher Wray used the term during remarks to the Association of State Criminal Investigative Agencies.

"You all know what’s driving the violent crime in your states," Wray said. "Whether it’s a community where a disproportionate amount of gun violence takes place or rival gangs wreaking havoc in a particular region or a handful of well-known trigger pullers who keep finding their way back to the streets, no matter how many times they’re arrested, at the FBI, we want to be your integral partner in the fight against violent crime."

Sayles said investigators did not believe the three shootings were connected and that none appeared to be linked to the deadly July shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival.

item.title: Adam Carolla credits Jimmy Kimmel for comedy career, warns society collapses when comics stop telling truth
item.description: Jimmy Kimmel was the first person to tell Adam Carolla he should pursue comedy, sparking a friendship that began with early-morning boxing training at KROQ.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Adam Carolla said Jimmy Kimmel was the first person in his life to tell him he was funny and should pursue a career in entertainment, recalling on Tuesday's episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" how the encouragement grew out of an unlikely relationship that began with boxing lessons.

"He wasn't a good boxer, but he was a good comedian, and he was the first guy in my entire life to ever go, 'You are funny, man. You should be doing this,'" Carolla said.

The friendship began with Carolla finding himself locked out of KROQ radio station, where Kimmel worked at the time, at 6 a.m. Eventually, Carolla spotted someone using their key card to enter the building, and he asked the man to relay the message that there was a boxing trainer waiting outside.

JEFF FOXWORTHY PULLS BACK THE CURTAIN ON COMEDY'S CREATIVE PROCESS FOR WHAT COULD BE HIS LAST SPECIAL

Twenty minutes later, Kimmel — who at that time was known as Jimmy the Sports Guy for the radio segment he hosted — let him into the building to begin their training.

"I ended up talking to him more about comedy than I did about boxing," said Carolla.

Carolla also touched on the importance of comedians speaking truth to power during the podcast, warning that society is in trouble when comics stop being able to joke honestly.

CONAN O'BRIEN, ZACH GALIFIANAKIS SAY IT'S A 'MISCONCEPTION' THAT COMEDY SHOWS ONLY TARGET CONSERVATIVES

"I think comedians need to sort of be truth tellers," he said, adding that during the coronavirus pandemic, "they got to the comedians."

During the pandemic, the comedian commented on facing calls to be canceled over jokes, criticism, and creative content. He has referred to those privy to cancel culture in both Hollywood and government alike as "cowards."

"Once they get to the comedians, we're in trouble," he warned Hannity on Tuesday. 

"Because you can get to the union guys because they're worried about their job, and you can get to the school teachers, and you can get to the politicians. You can get to about everybody because their job is to not get fired. But when you get to the comedians, that's a bad sign for society. And I was saddened to see that they had gotten to some of the comedians."

item.title: Rory McIlroy not bothered by Trump's expected appearance at Irish Open: 'Who are we to say no?'
item.description: Rory McIlroy downplayed distractions from Trump's expected visit to Doonbeg, calling the Irish Open host course an "Americanised" links layout.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is expected to make an appearance during the latter stages of this week's Irish Open, and while defending champion Rory McIlroy admitted it will make things a bit "different," he's not giving too much thought to the potential distraction.

Trump is set for a two-day trip to Ireland this upcoming weekend, and with the Irish Open being played at his resort in the County Clare village of Doonbeg, his making a quick stop and potentially handing the trophy to the champion on Sunday makes plenty of sense.

McIlroy, who has played golf with President Trump in the past, did not engage in any political chatter when asked about the U.S. President's expected arrival, but instead kept the focus on the golf and the task at hand.

"It's going to be different, but the one thing I'd say is his golf resorts have hosted PGA Tour events, European Tour events, LIV events," McIlroy told BBC Sport.

"He's a big fan of golf, he's a wonderful supporter of golf. He's got a beautiful property here in Doonbeg - it's the first time I've played it. I wouldn't say it's a true links golf course, it's a bit of an Americanised version of a links course, but it's still a great golf course and should provide a good test for the week.

"It's going to be different with him being here but we're here to play a golf tournament and it's a good golf course and keep our head down and play."

TRUMP CONGRATULATES RORY MCILROY ON BACK-TO-BACK MASTERS WINS: 'BECOMING MORE AND MORE A LEGEND'

"Obviously, there's a lot that goes on. So, logistically, it provides some challenges, absolutely. But at the same time, if he wants to come and watch the Irish Open, who are we to say no?"

Beyond Trump making a public appearance at one of the premier golf tournaments across the pond, this week's Irish Open could be viewed as a test run for future events, most notably The Open.

Turnberry, the well-known venue in Scotland, was part of The Open's rota of courses and played host to the major championship four times between 1977 and 2009. Trump purchased the resort in 2014, and the R&A, which organizes the championship, has not brought The Open back to the property since the acquisition, while consistently citing logistical issues as the biggest hurdle.
